why: Ranking titles A to E by revenue alone, skipping the division by editorial staff (27, 13, 8, 7, 2), gives D, E, B, C, A, the correct option, and sourceHas names only an adjacent-bar misread, not this slip; option A is the same slip applied to staff numbers.

$2,750 prices only the 800g can ($2,880, within 5%); $450 gives the average order in kilograms and forgets the price (432 kg, within about 4%); $550 sits above $450 at the same ratio as $2,750 sits above $2,250, the listed numeric filler (and is also the 800g order's 576 kg); the discount slip and the one-price slip land on $2,250, but sourceHas names both.

B multiplies by the scoop's weight in kg instead of dividing and also brings in s (two slips); C and D each need the three slips the two listed formula fillers describe (price-to-cost ratio, s, 1,000 or w on the wrong side), so they pass as the two fillers.
5.3% counts only scores 1 and 2 (38% x 14%); 0.9% is the answer off by a factor of 10; 3.2% has no slip at its precision but passes as the one listed numeric filler.

1, 2, 3, 4, 5 ranks by total order value or one year value instead of value per order; 2, 1, 3, 4, 5 gets the close Q3 ($30.9) against Q4 ($29.1) comparison wrong; 1, 2, 3, 5, 4 has no slip behind it and passes as the listed ranking filler.

$1,800 prices only the 500g bag ($1,890, 5% off); $9,000 multiplies by the 6 cases twice (about $8,800 to $8,900); $7,500 sits below $9,000 at the same 1.2 ratio as $1,500 sits below $1,800, the listed numeric filler; the discount slip and the one-price slip land on $1,500, but sourceHas names both.

3,250 hours counts the whole $47,000 total cost as the saving (3,357 hours); 2,250 leaves out the agency cost (31,700 / 14 = 2,264); 2,750 is the option just short of the answer, where a rough estimate (40,300 / 15 is about 2,690) lands under the threshold rule; picking the nearest option still gives 2,850, but sourceHas names that slip.
159 forgets the 95% step; 145 takes off the 5% twice (about 143); 138 continues a tight grid with steps of about 5% of the answer, where a rough estimate lands.

B compares total bins and forgets to put them per collection day (-4.5%); C reverses the direction and reads the average as every month; D adds the per-day skip to that reversal; dividing by November's figure still gives about 3%, but sourceHas names that wrong-base slip.

A is a near-miss figure (12% where the truth is about 8%; reading the industry line as Cleanova's profit and reversing the comparison gives about 13%); B treats the fall in the margin index (100 to 96) as the fall in profit; C rounds 18 / 4 = 4.5 down to four times, or reads a line a gridline off; the revenue-only, half-gridline and wrong-line slips keep D true, but sourceHas names all three.
